description: <div> </div> <div> <h2><strong>Some key info for you about Liberis: </strong></h2> <p>🌱 We were founded in 2007</p> <p>💰 We have provided over $3bn of funding to small businesses so far</p> <p>🚀 We have been named in<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>CNBC & Statista Top 150 UK Fintechs for 2025</strong></p> <p>🌍 We're a global team, with a dynamic presence in<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>6</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>key locations around the world</p> <p>🧠 We're a thriving community of over<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>290</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>innovative minds</p> <p>👩🏾 🤝 👨🏼 We're a vibrant melting pot, celebrating over<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>27</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>nationalities in our team</p> <p>🏢 Our team brings experience from over<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>740</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>previous companies, from startups to global giants</p> <p>🎯 We have just been named as one of<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>FinTech’s Finest 50</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>by Welcome to the Jungle</p> <p>💪 We’re proud to be an accredited<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><strong>Real Living Wage</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>employer, ensuring everyone is paid fairly for the great work they do!</p> </div> <div> </div> <h2><strong>The team</strong></h2> <div> <p>We are the Risk team responsible for managing the credit risk of Liberis’ portfolios, which include designing effective new strategies, managing the credit quality of our products across geographies, and providing specialist credit risk advice to the business.</p> <p>The Risk team is based in London and covers Risk analytics, Decision Science, Underwriting and Collections. This is an ideal role for an analytical thinker who is naturally curious, enjoys investigating trends and identifying opportunities, and is motivated by seeing their work influence real business decisions.</p> <p>You'll be comfortable taking ownership of projects - framing problems, conducting deep analysis, developing recommendations and working with stakeholders to implement change. While experience in credit risk is beneficial, we're primarily looking for an individual with strong analytical capability, commercial thinking and a track record of turning data into actionable insights.</p> <p>Reporting to the Risk Manager, you'll help shape Liberis' credit risk strategy by delivering analytical insights, developing portfolio monitoring frameworks and driving strategic initiatives across our global products. Our current analytics environment includes BigQuery and Looker.</li> <li value="3">The ability to move from data to an explanation: identifying patterns, investigating why they're happening and making practical recommendations.</li> <li value="3">Clear communication, including the ability to explain your own contribution to a project, your analytical approach and what changed as a result.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p> </p> <p><strong>Next steps</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>If this opportunity feels like the right fit for your next career move, we’d love to hear from you!</p> <p>Even if you don’t meet every requirement, don’t hesitate to apply or reach out to Chess (Internal Recruiter) on<span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span><a ---------- <p> </p> <p><strong>Our hybrid approach</strong></p> <p>Working together in person helps us move faster, collaborate better and build a great Liberis culture. title: Senior Manager, Accounting
description: <p>With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. </p> <p>Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.</p> <p><strong><strong>About the Job</strong></strong></p> <p>The Senior Manager, Accounting owns the completeness and accuracy of the global operating expense base across the profit and loss statement and related balance sheets for a fast-paced, global business. Operating within the Controllership leadership team, this role leads a team of accounting professionals and runs the global expense close end-to-end across all entities and time zones. The successful candidate will drive a comprehensive continuous improvement agenda to scale the accounting function through standardization, automation, and the adoption of enabling technology. This is an exciting opportunity to take full ownership of global operating expenses and help shape the future transformation of the accounting function to support significant organizational growth.</p> <p><strong><strong>Responsibilities</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead the end-to-end global operating expense close cycle under US GAAP, ensuring the completeness, accuracy, and timely delivery of all balance sheet reconciliations and reporting requirements worldwide.</li> <li>Deliver clear monthly and quarterly financial variance analyses to explain commercial drivers, risks, and opportunities while partnering with financial planning teams on spend trends.</li> <li>Act as the primary subject matter expert for operating expense accounting, applying technical principles and critical evaluation to judgment-intensive areas, vendor agreements, and commercial arrangements.</li> <li>Drive the continuous improvement agenda by simplifying, standardizing, and automating close processes through the adoption of artificial intelligence and scaling technologies.</li> <li>Manage and develop a geographically dispersed team of accounting professionals, establishing a high-performing culture focused on mutual accountability, clear goals, and career progression.</li> <li>Foster strong collaborative relationships with procurement, finance operations, and commercial partners to integrate commercial insights into accounting decisions and establish clear process governance.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong>Minimum Qualifications</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li>Professional accounting qualification (such as CPA, ACA, ACCA, CA, or equivalent).</li> <li>Minimum of 10 years of post-qualification experience in financial or operational accounting within a complex, multi-entity global business.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience managing the end-to-end financial close cycle, including operating expenses, accruals, and balance sheet reconciliations.</li> <li>Proven track record of successfully leading, coaching, and developing teams of accounting professionals.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li>Public accounting experience, ideally with a top 6 accounting firm</li> <li>In-depth technical grounding in US GAAP principles and corporate financial reporting standards.</li> <li>Strong proficiency in driving continuous process improvement, automation, or financial system transformations.</li> <li>Experience managing accounting operations and collaboration across multiple international entities and time zones.</li> <li>Exceptional communication and analytical skills with a demonstrated ability to translate financial figures into clear commercial insights for senior stakeholders.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong>Benefits and Perks</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li>Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year</li> <li>Focus on mental health and well-being: <ul> <li>Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth</li> <li>Company-paid subscription to Headspace</li> <li>Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Paid parental leave</li> <li>5 weeks paid vacation</li> <li>Time off for your birthday</li> <li>Paid volunteer time</li> <li>Focus on your career growth: <ul> <li>Development Dollars</li> <li>Leadership development</li> <li>Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings</li> </ul> </li> <li>Travel Discounts</li> <li>Employee Resource Groups</li> <li>Private health & dental insurance</li> <li>Income protection and life assurance</li> <li>Employee Assistance Program - including 24/7 GP & free legal advice</li> <li>Pension plan contributions</li> <li>Discounted gym membership</li> <li>Bike2Work</li> <li>Season ticket loan</li> <li>Social events & Thursday happy hours</li> <li>Free lunch 2 days per week</li> </ul> <p>The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.</p> <p><strong><strong>Work Environment & Flexibility</strong></strong></p> <p>At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. title: Senior Product Manager (Growth)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><a href="https://fin.ai/">Fin</a>, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.</p> <p>Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.</p> <p>Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.</p> <p>Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.</p></div><h2>What's the opportunity? </h2> <p>Self-serve is where the majority of our customers start their journey, and the Growth team owns that journey end to end. <strong>This role owns the self-serve</strong> <strong>existing business</strong>: once a customer converts to paid, the account is yours - through every stage of its lifecycle, as it adopts more of the platform, grows its usage, and deepens its reliance on Fin.</p> <p>Your mandate is to grow the value of the self-serve base: drive expansion, strengthen retention, and accelerate adoption of Fin and our newest products across thousands of paying customers. You'll own a book of business, a roadmap, and a cross-functional motion that spans product, lifecycle, data, and go-to-market. It's a rare Growth remit with a clear number to move and a lot of room to build the motions that move it.</p> <h2>What will I be doing? </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Own the self-serve existing business book.</strong> Own the remit end to end - from the moment a customer converts to the point they renew, expand, or leave - and be accountable for the net growth of that book.</li> <li><strong>Grow Fin adoption.</strong> Get more customers using our AI Agent across the existing base, and help the customers who already use it automate more of their support.</li> <li><strong>Defend and expand.</strong> Build the retention and expansion motions that grow the book - combining in-product experiences, lifecycle messaging, and a data/signal layer that flags which accounts need attention and when.</li> <li><strong>Connect self-serve and sales.</strong> Design smooth, well-defined handovers between self-serve and sales in both directions, so the right customers get the right motion.</li> <li><strong>Fix the key journeys.</strong> Partner with core product teams to remove friction on the journeys that matter most to self-serve customers - onboarding and activation, Fin setup and go-live, plan changes and expansion, billing and plan management.</li> <li><strong>Land new products & features.</strong> Drive attach and adoption of new products & features across the self-serve base.</li> <li><strong>Understand the customer.</strong> Deeply understand the customers you're serving through research, data, and direct interactions, and turn that understanding into a clear, prioritised roadmap you communicate to build alignment.</li> <li><strong>Build and ship.</strong> Collaborate with engineers and designers to ideate, build, and ship solutions, and leverage AI to increase your efficiency and accelerate product development.</li> <li><strong>Measure impact.</strong> Evaluate impact through quantitative and qualitative measures, own product quality, and model our company values and R&D principles in how you lead.</li> </ul> <h2>What skills do I need? </h2> <p>There is no minimum years of experience, and no need to have held the PM title. We care about your impact, drive, and potential - former founders, strategy & operations leaders, and consultants are as welcome as career PMs. The common thread is end-to-end ownership of a problem and the outcomes that follow. We'll be looking for evidence you've applied and grown these skills:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Growth and lifecycle expertise.</strong> You've owned retention, expansion, adoption, or monetisation for a self-serve or product-led business, and you know how to move those numbers.</li> <li><strong>Sharp customer focus and problem framing.</strong> You get to the real customer problem through research, data, and direct conversations before deciding what to build.</li> <li><strong>Strong data fluency.</strong> You're comfortable working with funnels, cohorts, and customer signals to find opportunity, size it, and measure impact - and you make decisions from evidence, not instinct.</li> <li><strong>Compelling roadmaps.</strong> You build and communicate a roadmap that makes the what, when, and why obvious to everyone who needs to align behind it.</li> <li><strong>Excellent product judgment.</strong> You balance customer needs, business impact, and technical constraints, and you know what to ship now versus later.</li> <li><strong>Cross-functional leadership.</strong> You drive outcomes across product, design, engineering, data, lifecycle marketing, CS, and sales - influencing teams you don't own.</li> <li><strong>AI fluency.</strong> You understand how LLMs and AI agents work well enough to assess feasibility, make informed product decisions, and use AI to accelerate your own work.</li> <li><strong>Outcome-oriented.</strong> You define success clearly, share progress openly, and hold yourself to measurable impact.</li> </ul> <p>#LI-Hybrid</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Unleash Your Potential</strong></p> <p>When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.</p> <p>In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at<a href="http://fin.ai/careers"> fin.ai/careers</a>. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. </p> <p><strong>Policies </strong></p> <p>Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.</p> <p>We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our <a href="https://www.intercom.com/careers">core values</a>.  </p> <p>Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. <a href="https://www.eeoc.gov/know-your-rights-workplace-discrimination-illegal">Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal.</a> Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.</p> <p> </p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Chief Customer Officer
description: Work from anywhere, impact everywhere Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world. Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country. To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job. We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow. We are committed to changing the way things are done. Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position Work from anywhere! Position overview Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible. The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision. The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against. This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep. The mandate Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would. You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved. Win the right members, efficiently. You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances. Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless. You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay. Build one Customer organisation, not four. Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call. You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations. How you'll operate This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here. You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them. You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title. You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach. You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger. You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom. What you'll have done 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime). Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either. Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC. Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app. Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage. Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite. A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove. The first 90 days Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board. Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads. Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week. What this role is not Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions. Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed. Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed. Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached. Other requirements A dedicated workspace. A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area. Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles. Why work for Xapo? Impact Globally, Work Remotely. Shape the Future Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world. Great work-life balance Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. Expect Excellence Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals. At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and eth

title: Founding Customer Success Manager
description: About Dust Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026. Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 . The Role We are hiring a Founding Customer Success Lead/Manager for the UK market . This is a high-ownership role for someone who wants to build a market and a function, not simply manage a book of business or an expansion. You will work with some of our most strategic customers, helping them move from initial experimentation to broad, measurable adoption of AI across their organizations. You will own the full customer journey, from executive alignment and implementation through long-term adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion. You will build trusted relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, help customers navigate the organizational change that comes with adopting AI, and turn successful customer outcomes into a repeatable Customer Success motion from our London HQ. As our first senior Customer Success leader based at the London HQ, you will help define how Dust serves customers from the office. You will create playbooks, establish operating rhythms, shape our approach to executive engagement, and feed what you learn back into the wider Customer Success, Sales, Product, and Deployment teams. Dust is an AI-native company, and that changes what Customer Success can look like. You will help customers understand how AI can reshape their work while using AI to make your own practice more effective, scalable, and precise. This role is suited to someone who combines executive presence with a strong builder's mindset. You should be comfortable operating without a finished playbook, making decisions with incomplete information, and taking responsibility for outcomes from beginning to end. What you will do Own a portfolio of strategic enterprise customers, building durable relationships across executive, business, technical, and operational stakeholders. Establish trusted-advisor relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, helping them define their AI strategy and turn that strategy into meaningful business outcomes. Lead complex customer journeys from kickoff through adoption, renewal, and expansion. You will coordinate the right people at the right time and make sure progress does not stall between teams. Drive measurable value realization by helping customers identify, quantify, and communicate outcomes such as time saved, costs reduced, faster execution, and improved decision-making. Lead executive business reviews and other strategic customer conversations, connecting product usage to business impact and creating a clear path to the next stage of adoption. Support customers through enterprise-wide change management, including rollout planning, governance, internal enablement, use-case discovery, and the transition from individual experimentation to organization-wide adoption. Identify and develop expansion opportunities across teams, functions, and geographies. You will partner closely with Sales to turn strong adoption and customer outcomes into sustainable account growth. Orchestrate internal resources across Customer Success, AI Deployment Strategy, Forward-Deployed Engineering, Product, and Sales to deliver a cohesive customer experience. Build the foundations of Dust's Customer Success motion from the London HQ, including account planning, executive engagement, adoption frameworks, value reviews, customer education, and feedback loops. Represent the voice of customers inside Dust by turning customer needs, use cases, and patterns into clear product feedback, strategic insight, and better ways of working. Contribute to the broader Customer Success team by sharing what works, raising the bar for strategic account management, and helping shape how a GenAI-native CS organization operates. What we are looking for You have 8+ years of experience in Customer Success, account management, consulting, solutions, or a related customer-facing role , with a strong track record of owning and growing strategic enterprise accounts. You have worked with complex organizations where adoption requires sustained executive alignment, cross-functional coordination, and thoughtful change management over multiple quarters. You have successfully managed senior customer relationships, including the ability to influence C-level and VP-level stakeholders and communicate credibly with business and technical audiences. You have a track record of driving measurable customer outcomes, renewals, and expansion. You can move comfortably between strategic conversations and the operational details needed to make progress. You have built or improved Customer Success processes, playbooks, or operating models. You know how to create structure where little exists and how to turn individual success into a repeatable motion. You understand how technically sophisticated products are adopted inside large organizations. Experience with AI, developer tools, data platforms, enterprise software, or another emerging technology category is highly valuable. You are fluent in AI concepts and are genuinely curious about how agents, language models, and automation will change the way companies operate. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should be able to engage confidently with technical teams and build practical AI fluency with customers. You communicate with clarity and conviction in English, both in writing and in executive settings. French is helpful because you will work closely with our Paris-based teams, but it is not essential. You have strong judgment, initiative, and ownership. You make sound decisions under ambiguity, follow through on commitments, and take responsibility for the outcome rather than waiting for perfect instructions. You are comfortable being both strategic and hands-on. You can lead an executive business review in the morning, rethink an onboarding process in the afternoon, and write the first version of a playbook when the team needs one. You are generous with context, direct in your communication, and committed to working as part of a team. You make the people around you better. What success looks like In your first six months, you will have: Built strong relationships with the key executives, champions, and decision-makers across your customer portfolio. Created clear account plans and adoption strategies for each strategic customer. Established a repeatable approach to executive engagement, value realization, and expansion planning from the London HQ. Helped customers move from isolated AI experiments to repeatable, high-value workflows used across teams. Identified the most important customer and market patterns and turned them into actionable feedback for Dust's Product and Go-to-Market teams. Created the first building blocks of a scalable Customer Success playbook. Over time, you will help make Dust indispensable to some of the most ambitious companies and define what exceptional Customer Success looks like for an AI operating system. Location We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together. We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect. That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call. Why Dust The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves. We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk. Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. Learn how we think and work. Our product constitution, a story about our mission Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human , Stanislas Polu , VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them. Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI , Gabriel Hubert , Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe. title: Product Marketing Manager
description: Hi 👋 I'm Chris. I'm a Lead Product Marketing Manager at hx - I joined over four years ago as a Product Marketing Manager. Outside of work you'll find me playing sport (badly), watching reality TV, or taking my dog Lucky to the park (or the pub!). Product Marketing at hx is a highly strategic function. We shape the company's positioning and messaging, decide where and when products launch, and build the process that gets them to market. This role comes with deep ownership over how we address our core audience: actuaries. You’ll need to go deep into the life and workflow of highly technical users and develop messaging, positioning, and content that neatly conveys the benefits of our solution. You'll need to be comfortable managing senior stakeholders and have great taste - but what matters most is drive, and a willingness to solve problems as you find them. In return, you'll join a team that's kind, supportive, and full of very smart people who want to go fast and far. If that sounds like you, read on! About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the team Marketing at hx operates at the intersection of demand generation, systems thinking, and constrained markets. We build authority and demand in a highly technical, niche space where every account matters. This isn't template-driven volume work - it's deep, strategic B2B marketing crafted for a known universe of accounts, and we stay involved from first engagement through to customer success. As Product Marketing Manager for Calculation Engines and Portfolio Intelligence, you'll sit at the heart of how hx becomes the obvious choice for actuaries who want to price faster and steer their portfolio with confidence. You'll own the technical story for our developer community - the most demanding audience we serve - and be the connective tissue between Product, Revenue, and the AI team, turning user insight into sharp positioning, useful sales assets, and narratives that stand up to scrutiny from people who'll know immediately if they don't. Your work spans two distinct challenges at once: deepening engagement and value realisation for our established Calculation Engines product, whilst driving launch readiness, early adoption, and strong feedback loops for Portfolio Intelligence. The team experiments constantly, uses AI to focus on strategy over busy work, and operates with a high bar for quality and pace. You'll be joining a group that takes work seriously but not themselves, where compressed learning is the norm and the most future-ready in your craft is the standard. Check out our Marketing & GTM Engineering Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining! What you'll be doing Drive deeper engagement and adoption of Calculation Engines among existing users, using the usage data we now have to spot where users stall and creating messaging and enablement that moves them forward. Own go-to-market execution for the Portfolio Intelligence release end to end - positioning, launch materials, enablement, and user communications that get it in front of the right people and drive real usage. Accelerate early adoption of Portfolio Intelligence by creating onboarding support and launch assets that help target users get to first value quickly, evidenced by users moving out of the beta programme into sustained use. Become the developer community's champion by writing technical content at a regular cadence that Solutions Engineering uses in live deals, and answering architecture and integration questions directly rather than routing them to Product. Build hx's position in actuarial AI by developing differentiated positioning and up-to-date competitive understanding that works consistently across website copy, enablement, and customer conversations. Establish strong feedback loops between users, Product, Revenue, and the AI team, so insight from launches, testing, and field conversations directly informs messaging, prioritisation, and product direction. What you'll need to have done Led product marketing in a B2B SaaS environment, balancing adoption work for an existing product with launch readiness for a new one at the same time - demonstrating commercial judgement across multiple GTM motions. Increased engagement or adoption of a mature product by using user insight to sharpen messaging or enablement - with measurable improvement in usage, understanding, or qualitative feedback from users and revenue teams. Owned a product launch end to end, including the internal readiness and enablement work that happens before it ships - not just the moment it goes out. Turned a complex technical capability into credible, differentiated messaging for a skeptical, technical audience - developers or an equivalent evaluator population - built on real user insight rather than generic claims. Worked hands-on alongside a Solutions Engineer or equivalent technical partner, comfortable being challenged on technical detail and holding your line, and earning trust across Product, Engineering, and Revenue without relying on formal authority. Used AI with real judgement about when a technical claim is actually true rather than just plausible, and applied that judgement to rebuild how systems like enablement, competitive intelligence, or win/loss work - not just run them faster. You're unlikely to thrive here if You expect full product maturity, clear roadmaps, and well-defined processes before taking action - hx moves fast and requires comfort operating in ambiguity where products, priorities, and messaging are still evolving. You focus primarily on flashy launch work or brand campaigns rather than the detail-oriented, outcomes-driven work of deepening adoption, engagement, and user understanding. You struggle to prioritise or make trade-offs without perfect information, waiting for others to decide rather than using judgment to move work forward with the context available. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. title: Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy
description: About Skyscanner Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻. Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍. Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here). Now, we’re on the lookout for a Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy to help us bring that vision to even more travellers. About the role (Hybrid) As our Principal Engineer for Identity & Privacy, you’ll shape the technical foundations that help us earn traveller trust while safely unlocking the data and AI capabilities behind brilliant product, personalisation, experimentation and advertising experiences. This is a senior technical leadership role with impact right across Skyscanner. You’ll own the technical strategy and set standards for identity, consent and privacy engineering across our traveller-facing products, data platforms and operational systems — spanning web, app, backend, experimentation, analytics, advertising and machine learning. What you’ll be doing Setting our technical strategy: You’ll define and communicate the long-term vision and roadmap for identity, consent and privacy engineering, aligning it with our product strategy, traveller trust goals and data and AI ambitions. Shaping identity at scale: You’ll lead our technical approach to purpose-scoped identifiers and consent-aware data processing across sessions, tracking, advertising, accounts, consent and derived identifiers. Connecting the dots end-to-end: You’ll establish how identity and consent state flows from web and app surfaces through backend services, event streams and data pipelines to downstream consumers — making a complicated ecosystem feel a lot less complicated. Turning privacy into engineering practice: You’ll translate privacy principles and legal guidance into reusable engineering patterns, platform controls, decision frameworks and measurable standards, including clear expectations around retention, deletion, masking, access control and auditability. Leading across Skyscanner: You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, Legal, Privacy, Security, Data Governance, Data Science, Marketing, Ads and Analytics to navigate trade-offs, create clarity and turn ambiguous problems into decisions teams can deliver against. Getting hands-on with the big stuff: You’ll provide technical leadership for large-scale initiatives spanning consent platform capabilities, privacy-safe experimentation, data retention and deletion, and traveller-trust features, while guiding teams towards simple, scalable, reliable and cost-effective solutions. Raising the engineering bar: You’ll use observability, engineering health and incident learnings to improve how we operate, while coaching and mentoring engineers and championing high standards, constructive challenge and inclusive collaboration across our Engineering community. About you Privacy-engineering experienced: You’ve translated privacy and data-protection requirements — including GDPR, PECR, CCPA/CPRA or equivalent global frameworks — into practical engineering decisions, working effectively with Legal, Privacy, Security and Data Governance partners. Built for scale: You’ve designed, built and operated large-scale distributed systems across identity, data platforms or adjacent areas such as consent, authentication, advertising technology or customer data infrastructure. An influential technical leader: You’ve led significant technical change across multiple teams without direct line authority, creating clarity, alignment and momentum when ownership is distributed. Strong in technical judgement: You’re comfortable making decisions where product value, traveller trust, privacy requirements, operational reliability and cost are all competing for a seat at the table. End-to-end minded: You can reason confidently across client surfaces, backend services, event streams, data products, ML features, analytics, partner exports and operational tooling — and understand how a decision in one part of the system can ripple through the rest. Practical about standards: You know how to turn policy into technical controls and measurable quality standards that teams can consistently use in real systems, rather than another document destined for a forgotten browser tab. Clear, collaborative and credible: You can create shared engineering practices, write clear technical strategy and work effectively with senior stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Legal, Security and Data Governance. Familiarity with privacy and consent technologies, experimentation, personalisation, advertising measurement, Databricks, OpenTelemetry or SQL is valuable but not essential — as is practical experience using AI tools to make engineering work smarter. What it's like here We are the real deal - no corporate gloss, no empty promises. Just a team of genuinely curious, caring humans ❤️, building things that help travellers explore the world a little easier 🧭. Skyscanner is made up of brilliant humans from every corner of the world. title: Head of VIP, Influencers & PR
description: About the Role: Reporting into the Brand Marketing Director, we’re looking for a Head of VIP, Influencers & PR to build TALA’s profile, cultural relevance and desirability through the people, partnerships, moments and conversations that matter. You’ll lead the strategy across VIP partnerships, Influencers, Ambassadors, Pro, PR, gifting and events, turning TALA into a brand that people see, talk about and want to be part of. You’ll know and understand that the fastest way to build awareness is to put TALA in the right hands, in the right places, with the right people. The successful candidate will bring a serious black book of relevant VIPs from celebrities and musicians to stylists, athletes, creators and cultural tastemakers and know how to build genuine relationships with them. You’ll be responsible for creating the moments that make TALA feel bigger, more culturally relevant and impossible to ignore. Tasks What You’ll Own VIP & Cultural Partnerships Build and own TALA’s VIP strategy, identifying the people who can meaningfully increase awareness, desirability and cultural relevance. Develop relationships with celebrities, musicians, stylists, athletes, tastemakers and influential cultural figures. Bring a strong existing network and continually build TALA’s VIP black book. Create strategic partnerships that go beyond gifting from organic product placement to collaborations, appearances and brand moments. Ensure TALA is consistently seen on the right people, in the right places and at the right cultural moments. Ambassador & Pro Programmes Own the strategy, vision and evolution of TALA’s Ambassador and Pro programmes. Define the role these programmes play within TALA’s broader brand and awareness strategy, including who we want to attract, why they matter and what we want them to deliver. Establish the programme proposition, structure, tiers, criteria and long-term growth strategy. Together with the team, build a best-in-class network of ambassadors and professional athletes who genuinely align with TALA and can become powerful advocates for the brand. Set the strategic direction for recruitment, relationship development, activation and retention, with the team responsible for day-to-day programme management and execution. Continuously assess and evolve the programmes based on KPIs including brand impact, reach, engagement and commercial contribution. Influencer Own the overall influencer strategy, defining how influencer partnerships drive awareness, cultural relevance, desirability and growth. Set the direction for the talent TALA works with, from high-profile creators and cultural tastemakers to emerging talent and community voices. Identify opportunities to move beyond traditional influencer activity into cultural partnerships, organic product placement and high-impact moments. Ensure influencer strategy is integrated with VIP, Ambassador, Pro, PR, gifting, social and campaign activity. Set clear KPIs and continuously evolve the strategy based on performance and cultural opportunity. Gifting Own the strategic direction for TALA gifting, transforming it from a reactive PR function into a significant awareness and brand-building engine. Together with the team, define who TALA should be gifting, when, why and what we want gifting to achieve. Oversee the strategy for key product launches, cultural moments, VIP gifting, stylist seeding and wider brand moments. Lead the team in developing, signing off and executing gifting programmes, ensuring activity ladders back to wider brand and campaign priorities. PR Together with the Brand Marketing Director own the overall PR strategy and communications agenda for TALA. Define the role of PR within the wider brand strategy and how it will contribute to building fame, credibility and awareness. Set the annual PR strategy, priorities, narratives and key cultural moments, working closely with Brand Marketing, Social, Influencer and Product. Brief the PR agency to establish the types of stories TALA should be known for and proactively identify opportunities to create news rather than simply respond to it. Ensure the PR team and agency has a clear roadmap and empower them to execute against it. Events & Experiences Own the TALA events and experiences strategy, defining how physical brand experiences can drive awareness, desirability, community and growth. Set the annual events strategy, including the role of VIP events, consumer experiences, cultural moments, product launches, retail activations and larger-scale brand moments. Define what makes a TALA experience distinctive and ensure every activation is rooted in the brand and designed to generate impact beyond the room. Identify and feed into the events team opportunities for TALA to create culturally relevant moments that can extend into PR, social and organic conversation. Oversee the brief and objectives for key events, with the team responsible for planning and delivering the experience. Oversee the evaluation of the effectiveness of events against awareness, reach, brand impact and commercial objectives, continually evolving the approach. Requirements About You We’re looking for someone who is highly connected, culturally switched-on and relentlessly ambitious. A strong existing network of VIPs, stylists, agents, managers, media and cultural tastemakers. A proven ability to build authentic relationships with high-profile talent. Experience creating campaigns and moments that generate significant awareness and organic conversation. Strong commercial and strategic thinking, understanding that awareness must ultimately contribute to brand and business growth. A strong understanding of culture, fashion, music, TV, sport, entertainment and what makes people talk. An instinct for what feels cool, relevant and TALA. Exceptional relationship-building and negotiation skills. The confidence to challenge the status quo and create ideas that haven't been done before. A highly proactive, entrepreneurial approach, you’ll spot opportunities rather than wait for a brief. The ability to operate at both strategic and executional level, from defining the annual VIP strategy to picking up the phone to a stylist. What Success Looks Like You’ll know you’re succeeding when: TALA is increasingly seen on the right people. We have a strong and growing network of A-list and culturally relevant VIPs who genuinely want to wear and engage with TALA. TALA becomes a brand that celebrities, stylists and cultural tastemakers actively want to be associated with. Our Ambassador and Pro programmes become recognised as some of the most exciting programmes in the category. Gifting creates genuine organic reach, conversation and product desire. Our events become moments people want to attend and talk about. TALA earns more high-quality PR and cultural coverage. We create moments that travel across social, PR and culture, delivering awareness well beyond the original activation. Most importantly, you help move TALA from a brand people discover on social media to a brand people know, recognise and want. description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142); font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">About Baringa </span></h3> <p>Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.</p> <p>The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.</p> <p>Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. We are growing our presence with leading UK health insurers and developing a cross-Baringa Health Insurance proposition. At the same time, we are building our Insurance Technology Transformation capability to support Global P&C carriers and clients across the wider Insurance sector.</p> <p>As a Director or Senior Manager, you will combine Health Insurance expertise with strong technology transformation experience, client leadership, programme delivery and business development. title: Senior Staff Engineer - Agentic
description: 📈 Who We Are: We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity. tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators. We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale. In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership. We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide. At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception. 🎯 The Role We're hiring a Senior Staff Software Engineer - Agentic to join our Agentic Service. Set the architecture for how we use retrieval, orchestration, MCP tools, identity and evaluation across agentic work. Help teams across tem build and operate their own agents well. 🛠️ Responsibilities Find the work: Work with Engines and Services to map how their processes really run, and decide which parts to automate, rebuild or leave alone. Design for reliability: Own the architecture across concurrent workstreams, with evaluation, access controls, recovery and human approval designed in from the start. Prove the impact: Instrument what you ship so the time saved is visible, and say so when something isn't moving the number. Raise the bar across tem: Codify recurring business logic into reusable building blocks, and help teams build and run their own agents well through design reviews, shared patterns and clear handovers. ✅ Requirements Must-Haves You own the problem as well as the solution: you've worked directly with business stakeholders to define what gets built, perhaps as a technical product lead, tech lead or engineering manager, and you don't expect a spec. DevOps or CI/CD workflows moved onto agents. Advanced retrieval experience, such as graph RAG or agentic RAG. 🎁 Benefits & Perks Competitive salary - our current band for this role is £117,850 or equivalent in local currency. Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission. 25 days holiday plus public holidays, with the option to swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and your birthday off. Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons. We can hire remotely across Europe for this role. Up to £1,200 or €1,200 per year for your remote setup. Up to £150 or €150 per month for wellbeing. 🧭 Interview Process First call with our Talent Team. Behavioural interview with the Hiring Manager. title: Senior Associate (European Competition practice)
description: <p><strong>About Charles River Associates</strong></p> <p>Charles River Associates is a leading global consulting firm that provides economic, financial, and business management expertise to major law firms, corporations and governments around the world. CRA advises clients on economic and financial matters pertaining to litigation and regulatory proceedings, and guides corporations through critical business strategy and performance-related issues. Since 1965, clients have engaged CRA for its combination of industry experience and rigorous, fact-based analyses that provide clients with clear, implementable solutions to complex business concerns.</p> <p>CRA's European Competition practice specialises in providing economic advice on matters of competition policy and regulation.  We assist firms and their legal advisors in all types of competition proceedings:  firms considering merger and acquisition opportunities or involved in merger control proceedings; and firms undergoing investigations relating to cartels, restrictive commercial agreements, abuse of dominance or state aid.  We also provide advice to firms involved in regulatory proceedings and sector inquiries. We offer assistance on the estimation effects of damages in cartel cases, international arbitration and intellectual property disputes.  </p> <p><em>For more information on the Antitrust and Competition Economics practice in Europe visit <a href="https://www.crai.com">our website.</a></em></p> <p><strong>Position Overview</strong></p> <p>Candidates will be expected to rapidly take on genuine responsibility, assisting Vice Presidents and other senior staff by providing conceptual and practical input to competition case work as required. The role brings with it the possibility of working on some of the largest and most significant competition cases in Europe, playing a key role in the shaping of the cases.</p> <p><strong>Desired Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>First degree in economics and a PhD/DPhil in economics from a well-regarded institution with a strong foundation in microeconomics, preferably with a specialism with large data sets (empirical PhDs) or Industrial Organisation and/or statistics/econometrics), plus up to 3 years of relevant work experience. <ul> <li>Non-PhD applicants should have strong academic achievement in a Master's program, plus 5-7 years' relevant work experience;</li> </ul> </li> <li>Professional work experience in consulting, business, or with a competition authority strongly preferred;</li> <li>Demonstrated understanding of economic concepts, competition/regulatory authorities, competition policy and quantitative and qualitative analysis methods;</li> <li>Exceptional written and oral communication skills;</li> <li>Demonstrated high level of initiative and leadership;</li> <li>Strong teamwork and collaboration capabilities;</li> <li>Excellent time management and task prioritisation skills.</li> </ul> <h4>To Apply</h4> <p>Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. To be considered for this position, submit through this job posting:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Curriculum Vitae</strong> – please include current address, email and telephone number;</li> <li><strong>Covering letter</strong> – please describe your interest in a role with CRA's Antitrust and Competition Economics practice in London and how this role matches your goals;</li> <li><strong>Writing Sample (optional)</strong> – we prefer a sole-authored submission from an existing work (work product, published article or job market paper) that includes your commentary on a quantitative analysis and/or relevant to the field of economics;</li> <li><strong>Transcripts (optional) </strong>- from the most recent academic training (may be unofficial copies).</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Work Location Flexibility</strong></p> <p>CRA creates a work environment that enables our colleagues to benefit from being together in the office to best deliver on our promise of career growth, mentorship and inclusivity. We celebrate diversity and we are committed to an inclusive work environment.</p> <p style="margin: 0in;"> </p> <p><span style="font-size: 8pt;"><em>The statements included in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. title: Founding Design Engineer | CodeSpeak
description: Role : Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff) Company : CodeSpeak Location : London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit. Job Type : Full-time About CodeSpeak Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away. CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years. Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece. CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift. What you are expected to do: Design and delivery Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform. Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result. Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design. Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team. Product problems CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it. Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model. In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review. Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them. Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open. Ways of working Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction. Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences. Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot. Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard. Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees. What you need to succeed: Craft You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own. You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical. You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages. You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software. You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users. How you work You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here. You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself. You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools. You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture. You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly. You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered. Nice to have A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well. Experience with complex data visualisation. Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder. A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this. What you get: An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks. A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic. An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists. Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead. Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years. A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance. Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you. Work in AI, a field most people want to be in. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
